Non-compliance triggers enforcement under § 96.380.

prompt.content: You are a ship's Captain, an AI command agent responsible for ISM/SOLAS/MARPOL-compliant decision-making. Answer accurately, cite the applicable regulation/article, respect the correct reporting/command procedure, and never omit a safety-critical step.

chosen.content: US regulation specifying ISM-related documentation requirements for foreign vessels operating in U.S. waters whose flag states are not party to SOLAS Chapter IX. First, carry on board valid documentation showing the company's safety management system was audited and assessed consistent with ISM Code (IMO Res. A.741(18)); Then, alternatively, carry valid documentation from the vessel's Flag Administration showing the vessel's SMS was audited and assessed consistent with the ISM Code; Next, alternatively, show evidence of compliance issued by a SOLAS-party government or an organization recognized to act on behalf of the vessel's Flag Administration; After that, ensure evidence of compliance contains all information and substantially the same format as a Document of Compliance certificate and a Safety Management Certificate. Use Channel 33 CFR 96.370, Channel 33 CFR 96.380 and Channel ISM Code (IMO Resolution A.741(18)). Use the prowords flag_administration, recognized_organization, company as appropriate. This follows ISM Code, SOLAS Chapter IX. Be careful: failure to comply will subject the vessel to compliance and enforcement procedures under § 96.380. Done correctly, vessel is permitted to operate in U.S. waters if valid ISM-equivalent documentation is maintained on board.

chapter_title: PART 96—RULES FOR THE SAFE OPERATION OF VESSELS AND SAFETY MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS
expected_points: Force majeure entry by a foreign vessel is excepted from the SMS certification requirement.
The SMS certification requirement applies to foreign-voyage vessels with more than 12 passengers, or tankers/bulk freight/freight vessels/MODUs of 500 gross tons or more.

prompt.content: You are a ship's Captain, an AI command agent responsible for ISM/SOLAS/MARPOL-compliant decision-making. Answer accurately, cite the applicable regulation/article, respect the correct reporting/command procedure, and never omit a safety-critical step.
Under what conditions will the Coast Guard deny my vessel entry into a U.S. port for lack of SMS certification?

chosen.content: U.S. Coast Guard regulation specifying when foreign vessels will be denied entry into U.S. ports/terminals for lack of a certificated safety management system, and the purpose of authorizing recognized organizations to perform SMS audits/certification on behalf of the Coast Guard. First, determine whether the vessel qualifies for the force majeure exception before applying entry denial; Then, verify the vessel holds a safety management system properly certificated under this subpart or SOLAS Chapter IX if it is engaged on a foreign voyage and meets the tonnage/passenger criteria; Next, cognizant COTP denies port/terminal entry to any non-compliant vessel; After that, to obtain a current list of Coast Guard-authorized recognized organizations, submit a self-addressed stamped envelope and written request to Commandant (CG-ENG), Office of Design and Engineering Standards. Use Channel 33 CFR 96.390, Channel 33 CFR 96.400, Channel 46 U.S.C. 3204(c), Channel 46 CFR part 8 subparts A and B and Channel SOLAS Chapter IX. Use the prowords cotp, commandant_cg_eng, recognized_organization as appropriate. This follows ISM Code, SOLAS. Be careful: no vessel shall enter a U.S. port or terminal without a properly certificated safety management system unless the force majeure exception applies. Done correctly, vessels lacking required SMS certification will be denied entry into U.S. ports/terminals by the cognizant COTP.

chapter_title: PART 96—RULES FOR THE SAFE OPERATION OF VESSELS AND SAFETY MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS
expected_points: An organization seeking authorization must document its internal quality system meeting one of three acceptable standards.
A list of qualified auditors and their operational areas must be submitted.
Foreign classification societies must prove reciprocity under 46 U.S.C. 3316 via a government affidavit.
Lack of the affidavit causes automatic disapproval without further review.
Successful applicants undergo an on-site Coast Guard evaluation per §96.440(b).

prompt.content: You are a ship's Captain, an AI command agent responsible for ISM/SOLAS/MARPOL-compliant decision-making. Answer accurately, cite the applicable regulation/article, respect the correct reporting/command procedure, and never omit a safety-critical step.
What documentation must an organization submit to be authorized to conduct ISM audits under this part?

chosen.content: A regulation specifying what an organization must submit to the U.S. Coast Guard when requesting authorization to perform ISM Code safety management system audits and certification under 33 CFR Part 96. First, submit a statement describing the type of authorization sought; Then, provide documents showing the organization has an internal quality system meeting §96.440 requirements, ANSI/ASQC C9001, or an equivalent Coast Guard-recognized standard; Next, submit a list of the organization's exclusive auditors qualified to perform safety management audits and their operational areas; After that, provide a written statement confirming procedures and records related to SMS audits/certification will be available for annual or on-demand Coast Guard review; Finally, if a foreign classification society, include a government affidavit demonstrating reciprocity under 46 U.S.C. 3316, listing authorized delegations to the American Bureau of Shipping; Then, await Coast Guard evaluation of the request; if satisfactory, the organization will receive an on-site evaluation visit per §96.440(b). Use Channel 33 CFR 96.440, Channel 46 CFR Part 8 Subparts A and B and Channel 46 U.S.C. 3316. Use the prowords coast_guard, classification_society, recognized_organization, foreign_administration as appropriate. This follows ISM Code, 33 CFR Part 96, 46 CFR Part 8. Be careful: request for authorization from a foreign classification society will be disapproved and returned if the required affidavit is not received. Done correctly, satisfactory completion of the Coast Guard's evaluation leads to an on-site evaluation visit as described in §96.440(b).

What are the five core elements a TSMS must establish and maintain under §138.205?

chosen.content: Defines the purpose and objectives of a Towing Safety Management System (TSMS) required for owners/managing operators of towing vessels under 46 CFR Part 138. First, establish management policies and procedures serving as an operational protocol for all levels of management; Then, create procedures producing objective evidence of compliance with subchapter requirements; Next, implement self-evaluation procedures to verify adherence to own policies and regulatory requirements; After that, arrange periodic evaluation by an independent third-party organization (TPO); Finally, establish procedures for correcting identified problems and facilitating continuous improvement; Then, demonstrate management responsibility by showing implementation and organization-wide adherence to the TSMS; Then, document organizational structure, responsibilities, procedures, and resources for quality monitoring; Then, establish document and data control procedures identifying controlled document types and responsible parties. Use Channel 46 CFR 138.205 and Channel 46 CFR 138.210. Use the prowords owner, managing_operator, management, third_party_organization as appropriate. chosen.content: Regulatory requirements under the Towing Safety Management System (TSMS) for owners/managing operators to designate shoreside responsible persons and to define the master's authority, including authority to cease unsafe operations. First, owner or managing operator designates in writing shoreside person(s) responsible for TSMS implementation and continuous functioning across management and fleet; Then, owner or managing operator designates shoreside person(s) responsible for vessel maintenance/operable condition and for emergency assistance to each towing vessel; Next, owner or managing operator defines the scope of the master's authority in writing; After that, master exercises final authority to make determinations on safe operations and to cease operation when an unsafe condition exists. Use Channel 46 CFR Part 138 (TSMS) - shoreside designation provision and Channel 46 CFR Part 138 (TSMS) - master authority provision (iii). Use the prowords master, owner, managing_operator, shoreside_designated_person as appropriate. This follows TSMS (Towing Safety Management System). Be careful: failure to define master authority properly could undermine the master's ability to halt unsafe operations. Done correctly, clear accountability structure ensures TSMS functions continuously and vessels remain properly maintained.

When exactly must I schedule the internal management audit relative to our TSMS certificate anniversary?

chosen.content: Regulatory requirements for conducting internal and external audits of a Towing Safety Management System (TSMS) under 46 CFR Part 138 to maintain a TSMS certificate. First, conduct an internal management audit annually, within 3 months of the TSMS certificate anniversary date; Then, audit all levels of the organization, including all towing vessels subject to the TSMS; Next, document internal audit results and retain them for 5 years, making them available to the Coast Guard upon request; After that, use internal auditors who have TSMS/standard knowledge, completed a recognized ISO 9001 auditor course, are not the designated person or responsible for TSMS development/implementation, and are independent of the audited procedures (unless impracticable given organization size/nature); Finally, arrange an external management audit by a Third Party Organization (TPO) auditor prior to issuance of an initial TSMS certificate or any renewal; Then, conduct a mid-period external management audit between the 27th and 33rd month of the certificate's validity period. Use Channel 46 CFR § 138.310, Channel 46 CFR § 138.315 and Channel 46 CFR § 136.112. Use the prowords owner_or_managing_operator, internal_auditor, designated_person, tpo_auditor, coast_guard as appropriate. This follows TSMS (Towing Safety Management System), ISO 9001. Be careful: internal auditors may not audit their own developed/implemented TSMS elements, compromising objectivity. Done correctly, properly conducted internal and external audits support issuance, renewal, and maintenance of the TSMS certificate.

What qualifies an existing SMS to be automatically deemed TSMS-compliant?

chosen.content: Coast Guard regulations establish how existing Safety Management Systems (SMS), including ISM-compliant ones, may satisfy Towing Safety Management System (TSMS) requirements, and describe the issuance, validity, and maintenance of the resulting TSMS certificate for towing vessel owners/operators. First, determine if existing SMS is fully ISM Code compliant under 33 CFR part 96; Then, if using a non-ISM existing SMS, submit documentation to the Coast Guard based on the initial audit and one full audit cycle of at least 3 years; Next, be prepared for Coast Guard inspection of SMS contents, audit evidence, non-conformity corrections, and vessel compliance records; After that, obtain TSMS certificate from a Third Party Organization (TPO) once deemed compliant; Finally, keep the TSMS certificate on file at the shoreside office and a copy aboard each covered towing vessel; Then, maintain and provide upon request a list of all vessels currently covered by each TSMS certificate. Use Channel 46 CFR 138.225, Channel 46 CFR 138.305 and Channel 33 CFR part 96. Use the prowords owner, managing_operator, coast_guard, third_party_organization as appropriate. This follows ISM Code, TSMS (46 CFR Part 138). Be careful: non-ISM-compliant existing SMS may be rejected or require modifications by the Coast Guard. Done correctly, iSM-compliant SMS automatically satisfies TSMS requirements.

chosen.content: Federal regulations (46 CFR Part 13) specifying the certification and endorsement requirements for personnel serving as Person-In-Charge (PIC) on tank vessels and tank barges. Use Channel 46 CFR 13.205, Channel 46 CFR 13.301, Channel 46 CFR 13.127(a), Channel 46 CFR 13.125, Channel 46 CFR 13.303 and Channel 46 CFR 13.121(e). Be careful: a course certificate cannot be used for a subsequent renewal of the same endorsement once already used for renewal. Done correctly, successful compliance results in issuance of a Tank Vessel-PIC or Tank Barge-PIC endorsement on the mariner's credential.

chapter_title: Inter-ship – MMSI of other vessel known
expected_points: An Individual DSC call with routine priority is used for inter-ship contact when the MMSI is known.
The MMSI can be entered manually or selected from a directory.
The calling vessel specifies the inter-ship channel for subsequent radiotelephony.
The called vessel must acknowledge the DSC call before the R/T conversation begins.

prompt.content: You are a ship's Captain, an AI command agent responsible for ISM/SOLAS/MARPOL-compliant decision-making. Answer accurately, cite the applicable regulation/article, respect the correct reporting/command procedure, and never omit a safety-critical step.
How do I set up an inter-ship DSC call when I already know the other vessel's MMSI?

chosen.content: Procedure for initiating a routine inter-ship VHF DSC call when the MMSI of the other vessel is already known. First, select Individual DSC call type with routine priority; Then, enter the MMSI of the called vessel or select it from the directory; Next, indicate the inter-ship channel to be used for R/T communication; After that, wait for the called vessel to acknowledge the DSC call when the radio 'rings'; Finally, begin the conversation on the selected inter-ship channel. Use Channel inter-ship channel (R/T). Use the prowords calling_vessel, called_vessel as appropriate. This follows GMDSS. Done correctly, conversation is successfully established on the selected inter-ship channel after acknowledgement by the called vessel.

First, make initial voice call on Channel 16 using low power; Then, move to an inter-ship working channel once contact is established; Next, if no response on Channel 16, call on Channel 13. Use Channel 13 and Channel 16. Use the prowords master, bridge_watchkeeper as appropriate. This follows GMDSS. Done correctly, successful voice contact established on an inter-ship working channel.

expected_points: A DSC radio sounds an audible alarm when a distress alert is received.
If no DSC acknowledgement occurs within about 5 minutes, a vessel able to assist should acknowledge by voice on Channel 16 using the Mayday format.
Urgency (Pan Pan) calls are announced on Channel 16 but conducted on a nominated working channel.
Safety information to HM Coastguard should use an Individual DSC call with safety priority, falling back to Channel 16 voice call if unsupported.

prompt.content: You are a ship's Captain, an AI command agent responsible for ISM/SOLAS/MARPOL-compliant decision-making. Answer accurately, cite the applicable regulation/article, respect the correct reporting/command procedure, and never omit a safety-critical step.
How long should I wait for a DSC acknowledgement before manually acknowledging a distress call by voice?

chosen.content: Guidance for small boat operators on how to respond to a DSC distress alert and how to transmit urgency or safety messages using VHF DSC radio procedures. First, immediately cease any transmission that may interfere with distress traffic and maintain a listening watch on Channel 16; Then, wait approximately 5 minutes for a DSC acknowledgement; if none occurs and you can assist, acknowledge by voice on Channel 16 using the Mayday relay format; Next, in the voice acknowledgement, state the casualty vessel's name/MMSI, your own vessel's name/call sign, confirm receipt of the mayday, and state what assistance you can give including ETA if proceeding to the casualty; After that, use any available means to relay the distress message to an appropriate coast station; Finally, for urgency situations, send a DSC All Ships Urgency Call nominating a working channel, then make the Pan Pan announcement on Channel 16 and move to the nominated working channel; Then, for safety information to HM Coastguard, use an Individual DSC call with safety priority and the appropriate MMSI; wait for Coastguard acknowledgement and switch to the indicated working channel; Then, if the radio does not support DSC safety calling, make a voice call on Channel 16 instead. Use Channel 16, Channel DSC Individual Call and Channel DSC All Ships Urgency Call. Use the prowords vessel_operator, casualty_vessel, hm_coastguard, all_stations as appropriate. This follows GMDSS. Be careful: do not transmit on Channel 16 in a way that interferes with ongoing distress traffic. Use the prowords AR (Personnel measures drafter), CZSK personnel, Directorate Personnel and Operations, mentors, mentees, reservists as appropriate. Be careful: the old job allocation process was no longer functioning. Done correctly, the reflection moment pilot was successful and will be incorporated into operations in 2021.

expected_points: Scheduled MRCC updates should use a fixed interval and consistent message structure including position, condition, and time to next update.
A single incident can progress through SECURITE, PAN PAN, PAN PAN MEDICO, and MAYDAY as severity increases.
SECURITE is for a sighted hazard, PAN PAN for urgency (e.g. loss of propulsion), PAN PAN MEDICO for medical advice requests, and MAYDAY for grave and imminent danger to life.
Calls must report immediately if conditions worsen between scheduled updates rather than waiting.

prompt.content: You are a ship's Captain, an AI command agent responsible for ISM/SOLAS/MARPOL-compliant decision-making. Answer accurately, cite the applicable regulation/article, respect the correct reporting/command procedure, and never omit a safety-critical step.
At what point should I escalate from a PAN PAN urgency call to a full MAYDAY?

chosen.content: Guidance on how a vessel should issue scheduled status updates to an MRCC and how a single developing emergency should escalate through SECURITE, PAN PAN, PAN PAN MEDICO, and finally MAYDAY calls using correctly formatted radio phraseology. First, when MRCC requests periodic updates, acknowledge and follow the fixed schedule (e.g. every 15 minutes) on the working channel using a consistent message structure (vessel name, position, condition, next update time, OVER); Then, if conditions worsen before the next scheduled update, call MRCC immediately rather than waiting; Next, issue a SECURITE call when a hazard is merely sighted (e.g. heavy weather developing); After that, escalate to a PAN PAN urgency call if the situation worsens to an urgent but not life-threatening condition (e.g. total loss of propulsion, drifting towards rocks, requesting tow); Finally, if a crew member becomes injured and needs medical guidance, issue a PAN PAN MEDICO call specifically requesting medical advice; Then, escalate to full MAYDAY if the vessel is taking on water and lives are in immediate danger, stating vessel name, nature of distress, persons on board, and request for immediate assistance; Then, always match the call level to the actual current severity, escalating or de-escalating as conditions change. Use the prowords master, mrcc, crew_member as appropriate. This follows GMDSS. Be careful: do not escalate straight to MAYDAY for a situation that is not yet grave and imminent. Done correctly, MRCC receives consistent, structured situational updates enabling accurate tracking of the casualty vessel.

What speed and maneuvering readiness is required under Rule 19 in restricted visibility?

chosen.content: COLREG Rule 19 governs vessel conduct in or near restricted visibility when vessels are not in sight of one another, particularly on detecting another vessel by radar alone. First, proceed at a safe speed adapted to the prevailing circumstances and conditions of restricted visibility; Then, have engines ready for immediate manoeuvre; Next, on detecting a radar contact with apparent risk of collision, take avoiding action in ample time; After that, avoid altering course to port for a vessel forward of the beam, unless overtaking; Finally, avoid altering course toward a vessel abeam or abaft the beam; Then, on hearing a fog signal forward of the beam, or if close-quarters cannot be avoided with a vessel forward of the beam, reduce speed to the minimum at which course can be maintained; Then, stop engines completely if necessary; Then, treat both vessels as having a shared duty to navigate with caution; do not assume a stand-on role. Use Channel COLREG Rule 19 and Channel COLREG Rule 19(d). Use the prowords master, officer_of_the_watch as appropriate. This follows COLREGs. Be careful: do not alter course to port for a vessel forward of the beam unless overtaking it. Done correctly, example given: own-ship detects a radar contact 25 deg off the port bow with a closing CPA; turning further to port would violate Rule 19(d), so own-ship should turn starboard or reduce speed instead.

chosen.content: UK retained EU law regulations set out the process for an applicant to dispute the outcome of a verification carried out under the Regulations, including arbitration referral and arbitrator qualification requirements. First, serve written notice on the responsible person within 21 days of receiving notice of the verification outcome; Then, state in the notice that there is a dispute regarding the verification and request referral to a single arbitrator; Next, attempt to appoint an arbitrator by agreement between the applicant and the responsible person; After that, if no agreement is reached, request the President or Vice President of the Chartered Institute of Arbitrators to appoint an arbitrator (not applicable in Scotland); Finally, verify the appointed arbitrator holds one of the specified qualifications (master/chief mate STCW II/2, chief/second engineer STCW III/2, equivalent certificate, naval architect, qualified person, special shipping experience, or CIArb member). Use Channel STCW Regulation II/2 and Channel STCW Regulation III/2. Use the prowords applicant, responsible_person, arbitrator, master, chief_engineer as appropriate. This follows STCW, UK Retained EU Law Reform. Done correctly, if the 21-day notice period is missed, the applicant may lose the right to dispute the verification outcome.

At what point in the survey process is the Certifying Authority required to issue the IAPP Certificate?

chosen.content: UK MARPOL Annex VI regulation setting out when a Certifying Authority must issue an International Air Pollution Prevention (IAPP) or UK Air Pollution Prevention (UKAPP) certificate to a ship following survey or flag transfer. First, carry out an initial or renewal survey of the ship's equipment, systems, fittings, arrangements and materials; Then, issue an appropriate certificate once satisfied the ship fully complies as at the date of survey; Next, for a ship transferring flag, verify an IAPP Certificate was issued and still valid immediately before transfer; After that, cause a survey to be carried out on the transferring ship and confirm its condition conforms with Annex VI; Finally, confirm no unapproved changes have been made to equipment, systems, fittings, arrangements or material since the last survey, other than direct replacement with conforming equipment; Then, issue the IAPP Certificate in English using the form in Appendix 1 to Annex VI, or the UKAPP Certificate in the form prescribed by the Secretary of State in Appendix 5 to MSN 1819 (M+F). Use Channel regulation 4, Channel regulation 5(1) of Annex VI, Channel Appendix 1 to Annex VI and Channel Appendix 5 to Merchant Shipping Notice 1819 (M+F). Use the prowords certifying_authority, contracting_government, secretary_of_state as appropriate. This follows MARPOL Annex VI. Be careful: unapproved changes to certified equipment/systems/fittings/arrangements/material (other than direct conforming replacement) can prevent certificate issuance. Done correctly, a compliant ship receives an IAPP or UKAPP certificate enabling it to proceed to sea without unreasonable threat of harm to the marine environment.

chosen.content: UK regulation describing the process by which the Secretary of State may survey a ship and issue, authorise, or endorse an IAPP Certificate under MARPOL Annex VI at the request of a Contracting Government. Be careful: discharge exemptions do not apply if the owner or master acted with intent to cause damage or recklessly with knowledge that damage would probably result. Done correctly, lawful discharge exemption applies if safety/life-saving, accidental damage with reasonable precautions, or Secretary of State-approved pollution response.

chosen.content: UK MARPOL regulation specifying which oil tankers of 150 GT and above must comply with Annex I regulations 29, 31 and 32, and the exemptions available for certain short, local, or special voyages. First, determine if the tanker is 150 GT or above and apply regulations 29, 31 and 32 of Annex I by default; Then, check if the tanker qualifies for exemption under paragraph (2): exclusively UK port-to-port trade, voyages ≤72 hours, within 50nm of land; Next, if claiming paragraph (2) exemption, retain all oily mixtures on board for discharge to reception facilities and confirm Secretary of State has determined adequate facilities exist; After that, check paragraph (3) exemptions for regulations 31 and 32 only: pre-1982 tankers ≥40,000 dwt in specified trades, or voyages within special areas, Arctic waters, or 50nm of land under UK trade or restricted 72-hour voyages; Finally, for tankers under paragraph (3)(b)(iii), retain all oily mixtures on board, confirm Secretary of State has verified adequate reception facilities at loading ports/terminals, ensure IOPP/UKOPP Certificate is endorsed for the specific voyage category, and record quantity, time and port of discharge in the Oil Record Book. Use Channel Annex I regulation 29, Channel Annex I regulation 31, Channel Annex I regulation 32, Channel Annex I regulation 2.5 and Channel Annex I regulation 2.6. Use the prowords master, flag_state_administration_secretary_of_state as appropriate. This follows MARPOL. Be careful: discharging oily mixtures without retaining them on board, when relying on an exemption, would violate the conditions of that exemption. Done correctly, qualifying tankers are exempted from regulations 29, 31 and/or 32 of Annex I, reducing equipment/operational burden for defined short or specialized voyages.

What must be included in the Operations and Equipment Manual for our crude oil washing system?

chosen.content: Statutory requirements for oil tankers fitted with crude oil washing (COW) systems under Annex I regulation 33, covering the Operations and Equipment Manual and operational use of the COW system. First, provide and maintain an Operations and Equipment Manual for the crude oil washing system; Then, obtain Secretary of State approval of the Manual and ensure it contains all information set out in the regulation 33.2 specifications; Next, revise the Manual whenever the COW system is altered, and submit the revision for Secretary of State approval; After that, crude oil wash sufficient cargo tanks prior to each ballast voyage, accounting for trading pattern and expected weather, so ballast water is only put into washed tanks; Finally, operate the crude oil washing system in accordance with the Operations and Equipment Manual, unless the crude oil carried is unsuitable for washing. Use Channel Annex I regulation 33 and Channel Annex I regulation 33.2. Use the prowords master, secretary_of_state as appropriate. This follows MARPOL. Be careful: ballast water must not be put into cargo tanks that have not been crude oil washed. Done correctly, compliant operation prevents contamination of ballast water and ensures regulatory approval is maintained.

What are my obligations for washings on a sub-150 GT oil tanker under this regulation?

chosen.content: Regulatory text specifying oil discharge and retention requirements for small oil tankers (under 150 GT) and for tankers carrying asphalt or similar products under MARPOL Annex I. First, retain all oil residues and contaminated washings on board the ship; Then, discharge all contaminated washings to shore reception facilities; Next, record the total quantity of oil and water used for washing and returned to storage tanks in the Oil Record Book Part II; After that, if discharging effluent to sea instead of reception facilities, ensure adequate monitoring arrangements are in place; Finally, for tankers carrying asphalt or similar products that inhibit product/water separation and monitoring, retain oil residues on board and discharge contaminated washings to reception facilities. Use Channel MARPOL Annex I regulation 34, Channel MARPOL Annex I regulation 34.6 and Channel MARPOL Annex I regulations 29, 31, 32. Use the prowords master, oil_record_book_keeper as appropriate. This follows MARPOL. Be careful: do not discharge contaminated washings to sea unless effluent discharge is effectively monitored per regulation 34 of Annex I. Done correctly, proper retention and shore discharge of contaminated washings prevents unlawful oil pollution from small tankers and asphalt carriers.

prompt.content: You are a ship's Captain, an AI command agent responsible for ISM/SOLAS/MARPOL-compliant decision-making. Answer accurately, cite the applicable regulation/article, respect the correct reporting/command procedure, and never omit a safety-critical step.
Under what conditions can an inspector board my ship under these Regulations?

chosen.content: UK regulations define the scope and limits of statutory powers for inspectors boarding ships to verify compliance with oil pollution prevention requirements under MARPOL-derived UK law. First, verify the ship carries a valid IOPP certificate (Appendix II, Annex I) or UKOPP certificate (regulation 13(3)); Then, verify whether documentation under regulation 19 has been issued and remains valid, where applicable; Next, investigate any regulated operation only if there are clear grounds to believe master or crew are unfamiliar with essential shipboard anti-pollution procedures; After that, verify whether oil, oily mixture, or oil residue (sludge) has been discharged in violation of the Regulations; Finally, inspect the Oil Record Book; Then, inspect the Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergency Plan, unless there are clear grounds the ship/equipment does not match the certificate or documentation; Then, exercise boarding powers only when the ship is in a UK port or at an offshore installation in UK or controlled waters; Then, for non-UK ships inspected under the 'clear grounds' provision, send the inspection report to the flag State's consul/diplomatic representative or maritime authority, and to any other Convention Party that requested the inspection; Then, when inspecting Oil Record Book entries, may copy entries and require the master to certify the copy as a true copy. Use Channel 1995 Act section 258, Channel 1995 Act section 259, Channel regulation 13(3) and Channel regulation 19. Use the prowords master, inspector, crew as appropriate. This follows MARPOL, UK Merchant Shipping Regulations. Done correctly, properly certified copies of Oil Record Book entries become admissible evidence in judicial proceedings.

chosen.content: UK statutory regulation implementing MARPOL Annex IV sets out the general prohibition on discharging sewage from a ship into the sea and lists the specific exceptions under which such discharge is lawful. First, determine whether the ship is on a voyage inside or outside a MARPOL Annex IV special area; Then, if outside a special area, discharge sewage only in accordance with Part A of regulation 11 (applies to non-passenger ships everywhere and passenger ships outside special areas); Next, if a passenger ship operating in a special area from the relevant IMO-determined date, discharge only per Part B of regulation 11; After that, if a UK ship in polar waters, discharge sewage only in accordance with chapter 4, part II-A of the Polar Code; Finally, assess whether an exception applies: necessity for safety of ship/persons, saving life at sea, accidental discharge from damage (with reasonable precautions taken), or discharge under a foreign State's less stringent jurisdictional requirements; Then, if sewage is mixed with waste/waste water covered by another MARPOL Annex, apply this regulation in addition to the other Annex's requirements. Use Channel MARPOL Annex IV regulation 11 Part A, Channel MARPOL Annex IV regulation 11 Part B, Channel MARPOL Annex IV regulation 1, Channel MARPOL Annex IV regulation 13.2 and Channel Polar Code Part II-A Chapter 4. Use the prowords master, flag_state, imo as appropriate. This follows MARPOL, Polar Code. Be careful: unauthorised sewage discharge into the sea is a statutory prohibition unless a specific exception applies. Done correctly, compliant discharge under regulation 11 Parts A/B or the Polar Code avoids breach of the prohibition.

chosen.content: UK STCW regulations specify certification requirements for ratings serving as navigational watch members, engine-room watch members, able seafarers deck, and able seafarers engine on qualifying vessels. First, verify that any rating forming part of a navigational watch on a ship of 500 GT or more holds a valid certificate of proficiency; Then, verify that any rating forming part of an engine-room watch, or designated for periodically unmanned engine-room duty, on a ship with main propulsion of 750 kW or more holds a valid certificate of proficiency; Next, confirm able seafarer deck personnel on ships of 500 GT or more hold the required certificate of proficiency per STCW II/5; After that, confirm able seafarer engine personnel on ships with propulsion of 750 kW or more hold the required certificate of proficiency per STCW III/5. Use Channel STCW Regulation II/4, Channel STCW Regulation III/4, Channel STCW Regulation II/5 and Channel STCW Regulation III/5. Use the prowords master, secretary_of_state, approved_training_provider, rating, able_seafarer as appropriate. This follows STCW. Be careful: a rating without the required certificate of proficiency must not be assigned to navigational or engine-room watch duties, or serve as able seafarer deck/engine, on a qualifying vessel. Done correctly, properly certificated ratings ensure the ship meets mandatory minimum STCW competency standards for watchkeeping and able seafarer roles.

chosen.content: UK STCW regulations specify mandatory certification and training requirements for seafarers before assignment to shipboard duties, covering high speed craft type rating, basic safety familiarisation, and advanced fire fighting. First, before assigning a seafarer to duties on a high speed craft built on/after 1 Jan 1996, ensure completion of type rating training per HSC Code para 18.3.3; Then, obtain documentary evidence (certificate per MSN 1740(M) for masters/officers) from Secretary of State or approved training provider upon successful completion; Next, before assigning any seafarer to shipboard duties, ensure they have received safety familiarisation and basic training per STCW Code section A-VI/1 and hold a certificate of proficiency; After that, before designating a seafarer to control fire-fighting operations, ensure completion of advanced fire fighting training per STCW Code section A-VI/3 and issuance of corresponding certificate. Use Channel STCW Code Section A-VI/1, Channel STCW Code Section A-VI/3 and Channel High Speed Craft Code para 18.3.3. Use the prowords master, officer, seafarer, secretary_of_state, approved_training_provider as appropriate. This follows STCW, Merchant Shipping Notice 1740 (M). Be careful: a seafarer must not be assigned shipboard duties on applicable high speed craft without completed type rating training. Done correctly, properly certificated seafarers are competent to carry out assigned duties, including on high speed craft and in fire-fighting control roles.

chosen.content: This excerpt sets out the statutory duty on the Secretary of State to periodically review and report on the regulatory provisions contained in these STCW-implementing Regulations. First, secretary of State carries out a review of the regulatory provisions in the Regulations; Then, publish a report setting out the conclusions of the review; Next, publish the first report before the end of five years from the Regulations coming into force, and subsequent reports at intervals not exceeding five years; After that, ensure each report sets out the objectives of the regulatory provision, assesses achievement and continued appropriateness of those objectives, and considers less onerous alternatives. Use Channel Small Business, Enterprise and Employment Act 2015 s.30(3) and Channel Small Business, Enterprise and Employment Act 2015 s.30(4). Use the prowords secretary_of_state as appropriate. This follows STCW, Small Business, Enterprise and Employment Act 2015. Done correctly, periodic public reporting ensures the Regulations remain fit for purpose and are reviewed for regulatory burden.
